A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EXGRA-MED and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Their content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v3 reports original medical VQA, chatbot, zero-shot classification, and ablation results, together with a clinician evaluation of generated captions.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark results and clinician evaluations, and additionally reports Qwen caption-generator and LoRA fine-tuning experiments in Tables 4 and 7.

M1.justification: v4 introduces an evaluated LoRA downstream adaptation, which v3 Appendix C only proposed as future work. The core graph construction, barycenter alignment, losses, and IMLE gradient-estimation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PMC-derived pre-training data, three medical VQA datasets, 193-question chatbot evaluation, 23 zero-shot classification datasets, and clinician caption study. The Qwen and LoRA experiments change configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark and ablation comparisons is unchanged. The new LoRA experiment uses the existing LLaVA-Med comparator under an additional fine-tuning setting; Qwen is a caption-generator ablation rather than a new competing medical VLM.

E3.justification: v4 adds a Qwen3-8B caption-generation configuration at 10% pre-training data and a LoRA-versus-full-fine-tuning evaluation on VQA-RAD. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, chatbot scoring, and clinician evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the generator-dependence analysis to Qwen, and new Table 7 tests whether EXGRA-MED's advantage persists under parameter-efficient adaptation. Existing component ablations, neighbor-count sensitivity, pooling analysis, qualitative examples, and clinician assessments are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practices are introduced. The existing feature-distribution plots and clinician-rating histograms are unchanged; the added benchmark results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds Qwen results of 70.13 on VQA-RAD and 84.7 on SLAKE at 10% data. Table 7 adds LoRA VQA-RAD averages of 71.48 for EXGRA-MED and 68.53 for LLaVA-Med. Retained numerical results, including the full-fine-tuning averages of 74.91 and 72.64, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph-distance definitions, metric and geodesic theorems, Proposition 1, Lemma 1, and their proofs in Appendices A–B are retained. Mathematical differences are typesetting and line-breaking changes, without substantive revisions to assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain substantively unchanged. However, v4's conclusion explicitly extends the stated weakness of autoregressive alignment from limited data to limited data and domain shift, modestly broadening the claim.

C2.justification: v4 interprets generator results as evidence of transferable alignment and discusses robustness under LoRA, its performance gap, and possible improvement through larger-scale pre-training. Existing architecture limitations are moved into Section 4.6; adapter-based future work is replaced by medical visual chain-of-thought directions.

D1.justification: The front-page resource link changes from a direct GitHub repository link to a project website. v4 identifies Qwen3-8B and reports 2.1B versus 7B in Table 7's parameter column, but does not disclose LoRA ranks or target modules. Existing hardware and core training details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Qwen3, S-chain, MIMIC-CXR, work on CT/MRI adaptation, and the MM-LLMs survey. These provide limited additional experimental and future-work context; the central positioning against contrastive learning, optimal transport, and LVM-Med remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.6 gains a bulleted analysis list and incorporates the former appendix limitations discussion. The clinician-study introduction is rewritten, affiliations are updated, and acknowledgments are added. Most of the main narrative and appendix exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: The document is globally reformatted into the NeurIPS layout, with a redesigned title block, narrower text area, resized displays, and widespread figure and table reflow. Figure 8 moves to a separate page, Table 7 is added, and Table 4 expands. Existing graphic content is preserved.

improvement.justification: The Qwen check and LoRA comparison provide useful additional evidence about generator dependence and practical adaptation, turning v3's proposed LoRA future work into a reported experiment. These are limited gains: the core results and proofs remain unchanged, LoRA implementation details are sparse, and the broader domain-shift wording receives no new dedicated test.
